newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sumitomo says not involved in alleged copper hoard.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo says not involved in alleged copper hoard.

text.p: Sumitomo Corp has no involvement with an alleged unrecorded stockpile of as much as 500,000 tonnes of copper in Rotterdam warehouses, a top Sumitomo executive told reporters on Tuesday.
Asked about a report last week on the possible stockpile, Sumitomo executive vice president Takehiko Yonezu said: "I have read the reports... It is not us."

The World Bureau of Metal Statistics (WBMS) released a report last week stating that statistics from 1990 to 1995 suggested a stockpile of 500,000 tonnes of copper may have been built up in Rotterdam during that time.
Traders and analysts were sceptical of the report, although some speculated that such a stockpile could be connected with Sumitomo's former chief copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka.
Hamanaka was thought by many traders to have amassed a huge amount of physical copper that he used to prop up world prices.

Sumitomo fired Hamanaka in June and accused him of racking up a $2.6 billion loss from unauthorised trades. Hamanaka was recently arrested on suspicion of fraud and forgery in connection with those trades.

Although several traders and analysts acknowledged the possible existence of a large unreported copper stockpile, the copper market largely disregarded the WBMS report as copper prices rallied Friday and Monday to five-month highs.
